leah: FYI prod alert — latency spike on m7b when sequences cross stride boundaries (noticed after kernel-selector tweak). p50 up ~1.6x for some customers. digging in.

riley: which kernel selector change? name or PR?

leah: PR #3421 turned on the new stride-aware selector that prefers FUSED_SW_ATTEN for windows with stride >= 512. suspect the decision boundary is wrong for mixed batch sizes.

omar: any repro perf profile? small reproducer would help.

leah: pasted quick profile from canary run (same model, synthetic workload, seqs 1400-1600):

```
profile summary: model=mistral-7b, seq=1536, batch=4, stride=512
kernel chosen: FUSED_SW_ATTEN
p50: 46ms -> 78ms (after selector change)
hotspots:
 - kv_tile_copy: 28% cpu
 - tiled_gemm_shard: 33% cpu
 - memmove: 18% cpu (lots of small copies around tile boundary)
notes: when seq < 512 or seq > 2048 kernel picks fallback GEMM_PATH and perf is fine
```

riley: hmm memmove and kv_tile_copy blowup suggests boundary misalignment. maybe the tile math is creating an extra partial tile that forces copies.

zev: could be the batch-slice heuristic interacting with stride; we changed slice rounding to roundUpTo(64) in that selector. partial tile -> extra KV memcpy -> cache thrash.

omar: any difference between warm and cold KV cache? i.e., first tokens vs later tokens.

leah: yes — cold-run warmup shows larger penalty. warm runs still ~20% higher than baseline. suspect pointer skew in KV indexing when offset % tile_size != 0.

zev: can you dump the tile indices for one request? also the kernel selection logs (`kernel_svc.debug=1`) would help.

leah: pasted excerpt:

```
[kernel_selector] seq=1536 batch=4 stride=512 -> choose FUSED_SW_ATTEN (score=0.78)
[tile_calc] tiles=3, last_tile_len=0x140 (320)  <-- partial tile
[kv_ptr] base_offset=12288, tail_offset=12504 -> misaligned by 216 bytes
```

riley: that last_tile_len looks suspicious — partial tile of 320 shouldn't happen if tile_size=512. where is 320 coming from?

omar: maybe a mismatch between head_dim alignment and tile_size. m7b uses 64 head_dim, if tile math uses head_dim*8 somewhere we might get non-512 boundary.

zev: hypothesis: the new selector doesn't account for `max_position_embeddings` clipping path (we recently added a soft-clip that reduces effective seq in corner cases). leads to odd tile_count calc.

leah: test plan I'm doing now:
 - 1) enable extra logs + run synthetic sweep seqs 480..2048 step 16
 - 2) try forcing selector to legacy path (env KERNEL_SELECTOR=legacy) to confirm regression disappears
 - 3) run small patch that forces tile_size align to 64*head_dim and see perf

riley: if legacy removes regression, we should hotfix revert the selector flag ASAP. canary -> staged rollback.

omar: quick micro-opt: when partial tile detected, avoid extra memcpy by using a fallback path that does in-place tail-handling. cheap to patch.

leah: agree. I'll test fallback-in-place and legacy revert. timeline: reproduce + fix test within next 3hrs, canary redeploy in 6hrs if green.

zev: also flag to QA: generate prompt mixes with sliding-window chat logs (many short segments in one request) — that's where stride boundaries hit often.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026. Owner: @leah. Severity: P2. Links: https://ops/redwood/incidents/INC-2026

leah: update: forcing legacy selector (KERNEL_SELECTOR=legacy) brought p50 back to 48ms in canary. good signal. implementing in-place tail-handling patch now.

omar: when you send patch, include small unit test that verifies tile_count math for seqs across multiples of 64/512/1024.

leah: will do. also added a quick harness to fuzz offsets modulo tile_size — turned up a couple other edge cases.

riley: postmortem items (short): 1) selector boundary test coverage missing; 2) batch-slice rounding change should have test; 3) add perf smoke with mixed seq lengths every deploy.

zev: agreed. also add metric for "partial_tile_count" in runtime telemetry so we can alert when it rises.

leah: final note: this looks model-specific because head_dim and kv layout matter. m8x7b might be fine but we'll run the same sweep. keeping this thread for rollout updates.

leah: (closing) patch deployed to canary at 1888887785, perf back to baseline. preparing staged rollout. will update incident once staged is live.
